set.dyndns.title: DynDNS
set.dyndns.subtitle: Routers and scripts update A/AAAA records automatically using a token.
set.dyndns.disabledByAdmin: DynDNS has been disabled by an administrator.
set.dyndns.adminEnabledHint: When disabled, /nic/update and /api/v1/dyndns/update answer every request with “badauth”. Tokens are kept.
set.dyndns.adminAllowPrivate: Allow private IP addresses (RFC 1918, ULA, CGNAT)
set.dyndns.adminAllowPrivateHint: Only useful for internal zones. Loopback, link-local and multicast stay blocked.
set.dyndns.adminProxyHint: TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is off: without the myip parameter, a reverse proxy’s own IP would be detected (and rejected).
set.dyndns.noZones: You have no zone with write access, so DynDNS tokens are not possible.
set.dyndns.maxTokensReached: At most {{max}} DynDNS tokens per user – please delete one first.
set.dyndns.fieldHostnamesHint: The token may only change these names – not the rest of the zone.
set.dyndns.fieldTtlHint: {{min}}–{{max}}. A short TTL makes new IPs visible quickly.
set.dyndns.fieldPtr: Maintain PTR in the reverse zone
set.dyndns.fieldPtrHint: Only works if the matching reverse zone is managed in the panel and you have write access to it.
set.dyndns.errNameTooLong: The name may be at most {{max}} characters long.
set.dyndns.errHostnameDuplicate: This hostname is already in the list.
set.dyndns.errZoneUnknown: Please choose a zone from the list.
set.dyndns.statusNoZone: Zone not (or no longer) in the panel
set.dyndns.statusForbidden: No longer write access to the zone
set.dyndns.rotateConfirm: Generate a new secret for “{{name}}”? The previous token stops working immediately.
set.dyndns.deleteConfirm: Delete DynDNS token “{{name}}”? Devices using it can no longer update.
set.dyndns.plaintextWarning: This token is shown only now. Enter it in your router or script.
set.dyndns.guideIntro: The token is sent as password (HTTP basic auth) or as bearer header – never in the URL.
set.dyndns.guideFritzSteps: Internet → Permit Access → DynDNS → enable “Use DynDNS”, choose provider “User-defined” and fill in:
set.dyndns.guideNoPassInUrl: Never put the token into the URL (no <pass> or <username> placeholder). Tokens in URLs end up in logs – they are rejected and the token is disabled.
set.dyndns.guideGenericBody: Server: {{host}}, path /nic/update, HTTPS, any username, password = token (HTTP basic auth).
set.dyndns.guideCurlBasic: dyndns2 with HTTP basic auth (token as password), with a fixed IP or with the automatically detected sender IP:
set.dyndns.guideCurlHint: Without myip the sender IP is used. The JSON variant returns details per hostname.
set.dyndns.guideResponses: good = changed, nochg = unchanged, badauth = wrong or disabled token, nohost = hostname not allowed, badip = invalid IP, dnserr = rejected by PowerDNS, 911 = server busy or error – the client retries automatically, abuse = token exceeds the limit many times over.
set.dyndns.guideHttpWarning: The base URL starts with http:// – the token would be sent unencrypted. Please use HTTPS.
set.dyndns.guideBaseUrlMissing: No public base URL configured – the examples use the current browser address.
set.dyndns.guideIpHint: Without myip the sender’s IP is set. Behind a reverse proxy this only works with TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true.
set.dyndns.result.nohost: hostname not allowed or zone missing
set.dyndns.result.badip: IP address invalid or not allowed
set.dyndns.result.abuse: token exceeds the request limit many times over
set.ptr.manageHint: Creates or removes the matching PTR for each IP – only in reverse zones managed by the panel. Existing PTRs pointing elsewhere are never overwritten.
set.ptr.noReverseZones: There is no writable reverse zone in the panel – this option currently has no effect.
set.ptr.lookupConflict: {{ptr}} points to {{existing}} – it will not be overwritten.
set.ptr.lookupConflictPlain: {{ptr}} points to another name – it will not be overwritten.
set.ptr.lookupNoZone: There is no reverse zone in the panel for {{ip}} – no PTR will be created.
set.ptr.lookupClassless: Classless reverse delegation (RFC 2317) detected – please maintain the PTR manually in {{zone}}.
set.ptr.lookupClasslessPlain: Classless reverse delegation (RFC 2317) detected – please maintain the PTR manually.
set.ptr.lookupForbidden: No write access to reverse zone {{zone}} – no PTR will be created.
set.ptr.lookupForbiddenPlain: No write access to the matching reverse zone – no PTR will be created.
set.ptr.lookupError: The reverse zone for {{ip}} could not be checked.
set.ptr.updateNote: The PTR of the previous IP is removed if it points to this name.
set.ptr.deleteNote: The matching PTR is removed as well if it points to this name.
set.ptr.reason.no_reverse_zone: no matching reverse zone in the panel
set.ptr.reason.classless: classless delegation (RFC 2317) – please maintain manually in {{zone}}
set.ptr.reason.forbidden_plain: no write access to the reverse zone
set.ptr.reason.other_target_plain: points to another name, left unchanged
set.ptr.reason.limit: too many PTR changes in one operation
set.ptr.settingsIntro: When creating, changing or deleting A/AAAA records, the matching PTR in a panel-managed reverse zone can be maintained automatically.
set.ptr.settingsAutoDefaultHint: Default of the checkbox and for API calls without manage_ptr. Each browser can remember a different choice.
set.layout.dyndnsProxyBannerTitle: DynDNS: reverse proxy detected, TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is off
set.layout.dyndnsProxyBannerBody: The panel is reached via a private address (probably a reverse proxy). DynDNS updates without the myip parameter then see the proxy’s IP instead of the router’s and are rejected; the per-IP request limits apply to all routers together. Set TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true (and TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS) if the proxy forwards the client IP.
set.layout.dyndnsProxyBannerDismiss: Hide this notice for this session
